executive_summary.conclusion: MCD is publicly crawlable and its rendered portal exposes clear routes to property-tax, online-services, contact, and birth/death registration tasks. The main observed discoverability risk is URL hygiene: session identifiers and HTTP handoffs appear in first-party navigation, while task destinations are split across subdomains; actual assistant visibility was not measured.

not_checked: Provider crawler access beyond public policy was not verified.
No actual assistant answer/citation runs, Search Console data, logs, analytics, or conversion data were available.
Keyboard-only, mobile breakpoint, performance, and form submission behavior were not tested.
Static collector reached its 45-second cap; two failed requests and capped landing-page extraction remain in evidence.json.
No authentication, OTP generation, payment, form submission, or complaint submission was performed.

readiness.detail: Public robots endpoint returned 404 (unavailable policy, not a block); inspected pages allowed named crawler roles by absence of rules.
Rendered landing and task pages exposed readable service labels, contact facts, fees, documents, login modes, and next-step links.
Four representative public-information questions were tested against first-party pages; required elements are covered below.
Exact-entity and task retrieval returned official MCD pages and task subdomains; no material contradiction was observed in the bounded sample.
Two safe rendered journeys reached public task endpoints without submitting forms; one exercised the birth/death service choice and retained visible guidance.

findings.title: Sessionized and mixed-protocol service links complicate canonical discovery

evidence.observation: Landing and service pages emitted first-party navigation URLs containing ;jsessionid=... and several key service links used http:// while the audited origin is HTTPS; rendered tax and RBD tasks hand off to separate subdomains. No canonical link was exposed in static records for sampled pages.

suggested_action.summary: Emit stable HTTPS, session-free canonical links for public task pages and redirect HTTP variants to HTTPS.
suggested_action.mechanism: Stable URLs reduce crawl duplication and preserve link equity while keeping service handoffs explicit across subdomains.
suggested_action.verification: Crawl landing and Online Services pages unauthenticated; confirm no session IDs in public hrefs, all public task links resolve to HTTPS, and each sampled page declares a self-consistent canonical URL.

proactive_opportunities.title: Publish concise task summaries beside service cards
proactive_opportunities.rationale: Online Services lists many service names, while RBD demonstrates that eligibility, fee bands, documents, and next steps are decision-relevant.
proactive_opportunities.mechanism: Add one-sentence audience/eligibility and document/fee cues to high-demand service cards so visitors and answer systems can select the right route before a cross-domain handoff.
proactive_opportunities.verification: For property tax, RBD, complaints, and licenses, verify a first-time visitor can identify intended audience and next public step from the service listing without opening multiple unrelated links.
